A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same patch-centric captioning framework, with matching authors, core formulation, and experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures, and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning experiments across four tasks, backbone comparisons, and supplementary aggregation, resolution, and modality-gap ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments involving LMMs, decoder architectures, ReLaion training, diffusion-based decoding, and learned aggregation.

M1.justification: v3 adds a Diffusion Bridge-inspired modality-gap mitigation variant alongside memory projection and noise injection. Section 14 also introduces a trainable attention aggregator combined residually with mean pooling and trained using region-level supervision. These are substantive additional procedures; the original zero-shot default remains.

E1.justification: v3 Section 10 adds ReLaion web-derived, machine-generated captions for decoder training and memory-bank experiments, substantially broadening the training-text distribution beyond COCO captions. The four evaluation tasks and their COCO, Flickr30k, and Visual Genome coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds SigLIP2 to the backbone comparison and IFCap and Diffusion Bridge to Table 2. New Table 3 evaluates Llava1.5 One-Vision (4B), Qwen2.5 VL (3B), and Qwen3 VL (4B), using visual prompting and cropping adaptations. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New experimental protocols include LMM visual prompting versus cropping, decoder configurations from 124M to 1.7B parameters, and one-epoch ReLaion training with matched or fivefold larger optimization budgets. The learned aggregator introduces supervised training on COCO traces with frozen backbone and decoder. Existing benchmark splits and metrics are retained; newly stated trace counts are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v3 adds decoder architecture/size ablations, training-corpus and memory-source comparisons, and learned-versus-fixed aggregation experiments examining transfer across captioning granularities. The earlier aggregation, resolution, and modality-gap analyses remain in renumbered Tables 6–10.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched original results, including v1 supplementary Tables 3–7, are retained. Substantial new results include T2D + Diffusion reaching 114.4 CIDEr on COCO Entities, and supervised learned aggregation reaching 73.9 versus 29.3 trace CIDEr while reducing VG v1.2 mAP from 20.3 to 17.8. These are results for additional configurations, not improvements to the unchanged default under identical settings.

T1.justification: The original region, trace, and memory-projection formulations remain. v3 adds mathematical definitions for the learned attention summary and residual region representation in Section 14, Equations 4 and 5. No theorem, proof, or substantial theoretical derivation is added.

C1.justification: v3's introduction qualifies the supervision claim around frozen backbones and absence of region-text training pairs, replacing v1's broader wording about requiring no image-level or region-level supervision. The abstract also removes trace captioning from its explicit comparative-superiority sentence. The central patch-centric unification and four-task contributions remain.

C2.justification: New sections interpret LMM regional performance through context and granularity limitations, discuss decoder capacity and possible overfitting, explain dependence on training-text and memory distributions, and identify limited transfer of supervised aggregation across granularities. The earlier limitations concerning fixed patch context, hallucinations, and supervised competitors remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents SigLIP2 patch extraction, LMM prompts and model sizes, ReLaion caption selection and memory sampling, and learned-aggregator training settings, including the initial residual weight and learning rate. It also supplies trace-benchmark counts and caption lengths and explicitly states that data and code are available. Existing core optimizer, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 substantially extends positioning through a dedicated comparison with image-text-trained LMMs, emphasizing regional control, decoder supervision requirements, parameter efficiency, and feature reuse. It also integrates newer captioning and representation work, including Diffusion Bridge, IFCap, and SigLIP2. Region-supervised LMMs remain outside the principal comparison.

P1.justification: The original narrative and relative ordering of retained sections largely persist. Changes include localized abstract, introduction, and conclusion rewrites, new Overview and Assumptions paragraphs, fewer Patch-ioner name mentions, and numbered citations. New scientific sections expand the appendix, but much of the retained prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. v3 adds Tables 3–5 and 11, an LMM adaptation figure, and a text-backbone column in Table 1. Figure 2 expands by redisplaying examples already present in v1's appendix; retained supplementary figures and tables are resized, relocated, and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new decoder, corpus, and aggregation controls make important design tradeoffs more assessable than in v1, while additional baselines strengthen the empirical comparison. The benefit is limited by incomplete integration: Section 11 retains broad memory-bank robustness wording despite Table 5's substantial memory-source sensitivity, and Section 14 emphasizes dense-captioning gains without addressing the mAP decline from 20.3 to 17.8. The added evidence is useful, but its interpretation needs qualification.
